Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & Context-window follow-up (FinCo)

Thanks for the time today, Tim — good conversation. Quick recap + ask so we can align on next steps (and get you a realistic SLO matrix):

Summary of FinCo requirements from the call:
- Context window: up to 32k tokens (worst-case archival retrieval + user prompt). Typical is ~6k tokens.
- Output: usually up to 512 tokens; occasional burst to 2k.
- Concurrency: target 40 concurrent requests at peak.
- Throughput: peak ~150-200 req/s sustained over short bursts.
- Streaming: yes — important for UX, must begin streaming as tokens are generated.
- Latency targets: business asks p95 end-to-end to be "snappy" — we flagged two target bands: 1) primary target p95 <= 1.2s for common/typical requests (6k input + <=512 output), 2) acceptable upper bound p95 <= 3.5s for worst-case (28-32k inputs). Please confirm these targets.

What we need from your side to size and qualify:
1) A sample of typical prompts and expected token distributions (attached is a sample_prompts.jsonl — please populate with a few representative examples).
2) Clarify how often you expect worst-case (32k) vs typical (6k) — is it 1%/99% or more like 10%/90%?
3) Any hard SLA must-have (e.g., "never > 5s p99").

What we can offer / what I will do next:
- Attached is a draft SLO matrix (FinCo_SLO_matrix_v2.xlsx) mapping token distributions to latency/throughput estimates.
- We'll run two focused tests if you give us sample prompts: (a) hosted run on our standard xlarge model to show baseline performance, (b) Dedicated plan projection with quantized model variant for cost/throughput.
- Recommend a 60-90 minute kernel-tuning session (Dev + Neha on the call) to validate streaming behavior and batching policy. I've linked a calendly below — please pick a time that works.

Next steps / asks:
- Reply with sample prompts or permission for us to test against a small subset of your anonymized data.
- Confirm the latency targets above (1.2s typical p95, 3.5s worst-case p95) or provide your preferred numbers.

Thanks — I'll put the SLO spreadsheet and sample file in the thread.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Confirmed: 32k is the maximum for a small subset of requests (mostly compliance/history-enriched queries). Typical interactive queries are ~4-8k tokens (median ~6k). Worst-case is rare (we estimate ~2-4% of requests).
- Output is typically 256-512 tokens; occasional long-form exports up to 2k (maybe 1% of requests).
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent at peak is accurate.
- Latency: The product team prefers < 1.5s p95 for interactive flows. For archival-long-context flows they can tolerate up to ~4s p95 if the UX indicates heavy computation. But we'd like to push for better if possible.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) With streaming on, can you guarantee token-streaming start times under 300-500ms for typical requests?
2) For worst-case 32k contexts, what are realistic p95 numbers and how much additional cost should we expect relative to a 4-8k context run?
3) Any recommendations on model/quantization/config that keep latency acceptable while controlling cost?

We'll get you a few representative prompts by EOD tomorrow. If you can share cost vs latency tradeoff examples in the SLO matrix that would help our procurement team.

Tim - thanks for the quick clarifications and for committing to the sample prompts. Based on initial internal estimates (Dev/Neha's take) and our test corpus, here's a pragmatic set of numbers we can include in the SLO matrix today. These are conservative projections and we'll validate with your sample prompts in the kernel-tuning session.

Scenario A - Typical interactive (median 6k input / 512 output)
- Model: rwx-16k or rwx-32k family (rwx-32k gives better long-context perf but similar latency for 6k inputs)
- Quantization: INT8 (L2) recommended for Dedicated to reduce memory + cost with minor quality delta
- Time-to-first-token (stream start): ~250-400ms median
- Median end-to-end: ~650-900ms
- p95 end-to-end: ~1.1-1.8s (we can aim for <1.5s with reserved Dedicated capacity and tuned batching)
- Per-token stream rate once started: ~18-30 tokens/sec depending on model and output length

Scenario B - Worst-case archival (28-32k input)
- Model: rwx-32k variant (32k attention optimizations engaged)
- Quantization: INT8 recommended for cost; FP16 slightly faster in some kernels but uses more memory
- Time-to-first-token: ~850ms-1.6s (depends on KV cache warmness and retrieval prefetching)
- Median end-to-end (512 output): ~1.8-2.6s
- p95 end-to-end: ~3.0-4.5s (we see ~3.5s typical in our tests for 32k inputs with Dedicated tuning)
- Cost multiplier vs typical: ~2.5-4x depending on sequence length and compute tier (main driver: attention compute + memory bandwidth)

Recommendations / mitigations:
- Prefix/KV caching for frequent history-heavy users (can reduce effective context scanning and bring p95 down substantially).
- Progressive summary pass: run a fast summarizer over the 32k window to shrink input for the main generation when possible.
- Route interactive low-latency flows to a Dedicated pool with stricter batching/CPU pinning; leave archival flows on a lower-cost pool with higher latency tolerance.
- Reserve capacity (Dedicated) for peak concurrency to avoid queueing-induced latency spikes - this gives predictable p95 behavior.

Next steps:
1) We'll run two bench tests as promised once you drop the sample_prompts.jsonl (please include 6-8 examples covering typical, long-tail, and export-like cases).
2) Book the 60-90 minute kernel-tuning session (Dev + Neha + your infra lead). Here's my Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood-marissa/finco-kernel-tune
3) I'll attach an updated SLO matrix after the first test run and share a short runbook for the tuning session.

If those numbers look reasonable I'll add them to the SLO spreadsheet and loop in our pricing/procurement contact for a dedicated capacity projection.

Best,
